name: knowledge-with-learned
message:
docs(shiploop): record build-a-small-single-player-battleship-8f4f83 knowledge at release-verify

Learned
- Tracing invalid inputs at the quality loop found a real crash that the first test set missed: a malformed request target (`GET http://[`) made `new URL()` throw in the request handler and kill the process. It is now a 400 and covered in TC-11 through a raw socket.
- Oversized bodies need both the Content-Length and chunked paths checked (413 in each).
- The page's async state needed review too: a New game press during an in-flight shot could mark the new board; fixed by dropping stale responses.
- An either/or status in a test oracle (413/400) is not an oracle; the spec was pinned first.
- `node --test --test-reporter=spec` with flat tests lets ShipLoop read names and counts.

Key considerations
- Choices the request left open, recorded in spec.md: fleet 5/4/3/3/2, 0-indexed coordinates, repeat shot and fire-after-game-over are 400s, unknown game 404, wrong method 405, body cap 64 KB, 1000 games in memory (oldest dropped).
- State is in memory and single-process; ship positions never leave the server (the game over response does not reveal them either).
- Local-only delivery: release was the guarded fast-forward return; nothing pushed or deployed.

Open for the next run
- Real-browser play of `public/index.html` was not observed (page logic was exercised through a fake DOM against the real server); the user is asked to open http://localhost:3000 and play once.
- Possible follow-ups, not requested: reveal the fleet when the game is over, a computer opponent that fires back, persistence across restarts.

name: raw-with-key-learnings
message:
Add single-player Battleship server, rules module, page and tests

Zero-dependency Node.js server: game.js (pure rules, injectable RNG, capped store), server.js (GET /, GET /api/new, POST /api/fire with JSON errors), public/index.html (10x10 grid), node:test suites TC-1..TC-15 run by node --test.

Key learnings: tests caught two real server bugs (page Buffer JSON-stringified; socket destroyed before replying to an oversized body); ShipLoop cannot read node:test counts so regression is keyed on test ids.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
